reasons: The backend change matches upstream. The existing-member check moves into `validate_target_email` with code `existing_member`, so a bulk request is rejected before any invite is created or emailed. The frontend also flags existing-member and own-email rows in the invite row and blocks submit, and it loads the member list on mount. The agent missed the initKea change that stops these rejections being reported as exceptions, which the request asked for explicitly. Onboarding is only partly wired up. So the patch is in the right direction but incomplete.

The backend change matches upstream. The existing-member check moves into validate_target_email with code `existing_member`, so a bulk request is rejected before any invite is created or emailed. The frontend also flags own and existing-member emails per row, using the members list and the current user, and blocks submit. However, the agent did not add the initKea.ts exemption, so these rejections are still reported to error tracking. That was an explicit requirement. The onboarding message and the failure-listener member reload are also missing. The main pieces are right but one stated requirement is unmet.

results.evidence: InviteRow reads `const existingMemberError = inviteRowErrors[index]` and applies it to the email input: `className={`error-on-blur${!invitesToSend[index]?.isValid || existingMemberError ? ' errored' : ''}`}`, plus an inline message `{existingMemberError && <LemonField.Error error={existingMemberError} />}`. `inviteRowErrors` is a selector over `invitesToSend`, so it updates as the user types, before any submit: `return existingMemberEmails.has(email) ? EXISTING_MEMBER_INVITE_ERROR : null`. InviteModal renders `<InviteTeamMatesComponent />`, which renders these rows.

In the `inviteRowErrors` selector: `if (user?.email && email === user.email.toLowerCase()) { return OWN_EMAIL_INVITE_ERROR }`. This feeds the same row error used for the errored class, the `LemonField.Error`, and `canSubmit` / `existingMemberDisabledReason`.

The settings dialog is covered: `disabledReason={userCannotInvite ? ... : (existingMemberDisabledReason ?? (!canSubmit ? 'Please fill out all fields' : undefined))}`, and the per-row button has `disabledReason={existingMemberError ?? undefined}`. The onboarding step is not: the patch only adds `existingMemberDisabledReason` to the destructuring in OnboardingInviteTeammates.tsx and never uses it. `continueDisabledReason` is unchanged and falls through to `: !canSubmitInvites ? 'Please fill out all fields' : undefined`, so the control is disabled but the reason says nothing about existing members.

Row side: `const email = target_email.trim().toLowerCase()`. Member side: `new Set((members ?? []).map(({ user }) => user.email.toLowerCase()))`. ' Rose.Dawson@PostHog.com' becomes 'rose.dawson@posthog.com' and matches the set entry.

InviteTeamMatesComponent (used by both the modal and onboarding) does `const { ensureAllMembersLoaded } = useActions(membersLogic)` and `useOnMountEffect(ensureAllMembersLoaded)`. The own-email check does not depend on members: `existingMemberEmails` falls back to `(members ?? [])`, and the `user?.email` comparison runs before the set lookup. membersLogic itself is not shown, so this assumes `ensureAllMembersLoaded` exists there as the patch uses it.

The membership check moved from `create()` into field validation: `validate_target_email` now calls `validate_invite_target_email_is_not_member(self.context["organization_id"], email)`, and the old check in `create` was removed. It raises `exceptions.ValidationError(...)`, which is a 400. The bulk view is not shown, but `first_bulk_invite_error` documents 'A many=True error is a list of per-row dicts', indicating the bulk path validates all rows through a many=True serializer before any `create()` (which is where invites are created and `send_invite` is called).

`raise exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="existing_member")` is raised from `validate_target_email`, so DRF attributes it to the `target_email` field. For bulk, `first_bulk_invite_error` re-raises `exceptions.ValidationError(row_errors)` using the per-row dict, which keeps the field key and the ErrorDetail code. The bulk view and exception handler are not shown, so the final response shape is inferred.

Nothing in the patch touches error reporting on the submit path. The `inviteTeamMembers` loader is unchanged (`return await api.create<OrganizationInviteType[]>(...)`) with no try/catch or code check, and the `listeners` block only has `inviteTeamMembersSuccess` and `addProjectAccess`. There is no `inviteTeamMembersFailure` handling and no branch on the `existing_member` code, so the rejection is handled exactly as before.

There is no failure listener in inviteLogic: `listeners` contains only `inviteTeamMembersSuccess` and `addProjectAccess`. Nothing reloads members after a server rejection; the only member load is `useOnMountEffect(ensureAllMembersLoaded)` when the form mounts, so a row unknown to the client stays unflagged after the rejection.

InviteRow adds `existingMemberError = inviteRowErrors[index]`, applies ' errored' class to the email input and renders `<LemonField.Error error={existingMemberError} />`; inviteRowErrors is derived from membersLogic members.

The modal footer uses `existingMemberDisabledReason ?? ...`, and the per-row button has `disabledReason={existingMemberError ?? undefined}`. In OnboardingInviteTeammates, `existingMemberDisabledReason` is only destructured and never used; `continueDisabledReason` still falls to 'Please fill out all fields' when canSubmit is false. So the onboarding submit doesn't communicate the members reason.
Row email is `target_email.trim().toLowerCase()` and member emails are stored with `user.email.toLowerCase()` in the Set.
`useOnMountEffect(ensureAllMembersLoaded)` in InviteTeamMatesComponent; own-email check depends only on `user`, so it applies before members load.
The check moved from create() into `validate_target_email` via `validate_invite_target_email_is_not_member`, so bulk validation of every row happens before any create().

`raise exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="existing_member")` inside validate_target_email, which DRF attributes to the target_email field.
No change touches error-tracking/exception capture for the invite submission path; no listener or handling in inviteLogic filters existing_member failures.
inviteLogic has no inviteTeamMembersFailure listener that reloads members; listeners only handle success and addProjectAccess.
